newsitem.title: USA: Reuters shows interest in Dow Jones - report.
newsitem.headline: Reuters shows interest in Dow Jones - report.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc has expressed interest in either buying, merging with or forming a joint venture with its rival Dow Jones & Co Inc, according to a U.S. business news magazine.

In its February 10 issue released on Thursday, Business Week said Reuters, the news and information company, had approached some of the controlling shareholders of Dow Jones expressing interest in making a deal.
A spokesman for Reuters declined on Thursday to comment on the report, which appeared in the "Inside Wall Street" column.
"Reuters never addresses speculation or rumour of this sort," said spokesman Robert Crooke. "It always looks at opportunities but never comments on them."
Dow Jones spokesman Roger May said "that's our standard response too."
Calling the column "pure speculation," May told Reuters the "controlling shareholders" referred to descendants of founder Clarence Barron, adding "it isn't (the company) directly."
The column cited an unidentified investment banker and money managers as saying that Reuters had told the shareholders that it would not do anything hostile.

"Some money managers say that Reuters Holdings ... has sent feelers to some of the controlling DJ (Dow Jones) shareholders about their interest in a merger, joint venture, or an outright sale of Dow Jones," it said.
"Reuters ... emphasised in its feelers that it won't do anything hostile," it added.
Dow Jones reported earlier this month that it planned to spend $650 million to expand and revitalise its Telerate financial information services unit.
Dow Jones also owns the daily financial newspaper, The Wall Street Journal.
